licenseNote: Original structured descriptions created for AgriGuardian X. Linked external sources retain their own terms.
safetyBoundary: Visual signs support scouting only. Confirm through field history, crop stage, laboratory testing or a qualified local expert before treatment.

records.name: Early leaf spot
symptoms: Brown circular spots, often with a yellow halo
Lesions may appear first on older leaves
records.confirm: Compare both leaf surfaces and lesion development across rows; rule out late leaf spot and nutrient injury.
actions: Use only locally verified IPM guidance

records.name: Late leaf spot
symptoms: Dark brown to black circular lesions
records.confirm: Inspect lesion colour and lower-leaf surface and obtain local plant-pathology confirmation.
actions: Reduce prolonged leaf wetness where possible

records.name: Rust
symptoms: Orange-brown pustules, commonly on lower leaf surfaces
Yellowing and early leaf fall when severe
records.confirm: Rub-check pustules carefully and distinguish them from soil splash and leaf spots.
actions: Use local IPM advice before fungicide selection

records.name: Stem rot
symptoms: White fungal growth near soil line
records.confirm: Inspect crown and nearby plants; confirm the causal organism before treatment.
actions: Use clean seed and rotation guidance

records.name: Leaf miner
symptoms: Folded leaflets with larvae or webbing
records.confirm: Open several fresh mines and count active larvae and natural enemies.
actions: Treat only labelled crop-pest uses when required

records.name: Aphid
symptoms: Curling, sticky honeydew and possible virus risk
records.confirm: Check undersides, colony density and ladybird/lacewing activity.

records.name: White grub
symptoms: Patchy wilting and plants that pull out easily
records.confirm: Dig around newly wilted plants and count grubs per sampling point.
actions: Use adult monitoring and cultural controls

records.name: Turcicum leaf blight
symptoms: Long cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions
Lesions expand and merge under humid conditions
records.confirm: Compare lesion shape and crop stage; obtain local confirmation.
actions: Use tolerant varieties in future seasons
Rotate fungicide groups only when locally advised

records.name: Downy mildew
symptoms: Stunting and abnormal tassel or ear development
records.confirm: Check early-morning growth and confirm against nutrient banding.
actions: Remove severely affected plants where advised

records.name: Stalk rot complex
symptoms: Weak lower stalk and premature drying
Plants lodge and pith may discolor
records.confirm: Use pinch/push tests and split representative stalks.

records.name: Fall armyworm
symptoms: Window-pane feeding and ragged whorl leaves
Larva may show an inverted Y mark on the head
records.confirm: Inspect multiple whorls for live larvae, frass and natural enemies.
actions: Direct any labelled treatment into the whorl only as instructed

records.name: Stem borer
symptoms: Dead heart or tunnelling in the stem
records.confirm: Check whorl damage and split selected stems to find larvae or galleries.
actions: Remove heavily infested residues where recommended

records.name: Bacterial blight
records.confirm: Compare angular vein-bounded lesions and confirm through a diagnostic service.
actions: Avoid field work when foliage is wet

records.name: Wilt complex
symptoms: Internal vascular discoloration may be present
records.confirm: Cut the lower stem and assess roots, soil moisture and nematode risk.

records.name: Cotton leaf curl disease
symptoms: Upward or downward curling and vein thickening
records.confirm: Check whitefly presence and distinguish herbicide or nutrient injury.
actions: Do not select chemicals from symptoms alone

records.name: Cotton bollworm
symptoms: Feeding holes, frass and damaged squares or bolls
Larvae may be present partly inside fruiting bodies
records.confirm: Count larvae and damaged fruiting bodies at fixed field points.
actions: Rotate IRAC groups only when treatment is justified

records.name: Pink bollworm
symptoms: Rosette flowers and internal boll feeding
Exit holes may be absent in early damage
records.confirm: Open sampled green bolls and use pheromone monitoring.
actions: Follow timely harvest and residue destruction guidance
Use approved refuge and resistance practices

records.name: Whitefly
symptoms: Adults and nymphs on leaf undersides
Honeydew, sooty mould and virus transmission risk
records.confirm: Count adults on standard leaves and inspect nymphs/natural enemies.
actions: Use local thresholds and labelled options

records.name: Cotton aphid
symptoms: Dense colonies and curled tender leaves
records.confirm: Count colonies and beneficial insects on representative plants.

records.name: Rice blast
symptoms: Neck infection can cause white or poorly filled panicles
records.confirm: Identify lesion form and crop stage and obtain local confirmation.
actions: Follow FRAC rotation and local advisories

records.name: Sheath blight
symptoms: Oval green-grey lesions beginning near water level
Lesions expand upward in dense canopies
records.confirm: Inspect humid dense patches and distinguish from other sheath diseases.
actions: Avoid excessive plant density and nitrogen

records.name: Bacterial leaf blight
symptoms: Water-soaked streaks from leaf tips or margins
Yellowing and drying along wavy lesion edges
records.confirm: Use field history and diagnostic confirmation; do not confuse with nutrient scorch.
actions: Use clean seed and resistant varieties

records.name: Yellow stem borer
records.confirm: Pull affected central shoots and inspect for boring signs or larvae.

records.name: Brown planthopper
records.confirm: Part plants at several points and count insects and predators at the base.
actions: Avoid excess nitrogen and continuous flooding where locally advised

records.name: Early blight
symptoms: Lower leaves usually show symptoms first
records.confirm: Compare lesion rings, leaf age and spread pattern.
actions: Remove badly affected lower foliage safely
Use local IPM and resistance management

records.name: Late blight
symptoms: Rapid browning under cool humid conditions
records.confirm: Photograph both leaf surfaces and check nearby plants for rapid spread.

records.name: Bacterial wilt
symptoms: Sudden wilt while leaves may remain green
records.confirm: Use a stem-streaming test only as a screen and obtain diagnostic confirmation.
actions: Avoid moving contaminated soil or water
Use rotation and resistant rootstock guidance

records.name: Tomato leaf curl disease
symptoms: Severe leaf curling and reduced leaf size
records.confirm: Check whitefly vector pressure and distinguish from mites or herbicide injury.
actions: Remove severely affected young plants where advised

records.name: Tomato fruit borer
symptoms: Round feeding holes and frass on fruit
records.confirm: Count larvae and damaged flowers/fruits at fixed plants.

records.name: Whitefly
symptoms: Adults fly up when plants are disturbed
records.confirm: Inspect undersides and use yellow traps only as monitoring support.

records.name: Leaf miner
records.confirm: Count active mines separately from old empty damage.

records.name: Anthracnose / fruit rot
symptoms: Dark spore masses may develop in humid weather
records.confirm: Inspect fruit at multiple stages and confirm the pathogen locally.
actions: Manage canopy moisture and rotate FRAC groups

records.name: Powdery mildew
symptoms: Powdery growth often on lower leaf surfaces
records.confirm: Check both surfaces and distinguish from dust or mite damage.

records.name: Chilli leaf curl complex
records.confirm: Assess thrips, mites and whiteflies and obtain diagnostic support.
actions: Do not diagnose the cause from curl alone

records.name: Thrips
symptoms: Tiny slender insects in tender tissue
records.confirm: Tap flowers/leaves over white paper and count thrips and predators.

records.name: Broad/yellow mite
symptoms: Downward curling and hardened narrow leaves
records.confirm: Use magnification and distinguish mites from thrips and viral symptoms.

records.name: Nitrogen deficiency
symptoms: General pale green colour beginning on older leaves
records.confirm: Compare old and young leaves and confirm with soil or tissue analysis.
actions: Avoid adding urea from colour alone

records.name: Phosphorus deficiency
symptoms: Purple or reddish colour may appear in some crops
records.confirm: Test soil phosphorus and review pH, temperature and root health.

records.name: Potassium deficiency
symptoms: Weak stems and reduced stress tolerance
records.confirm: Confirm tissue/soil potassium and rule out salinity or drought.

records.name: Calcium deficiency
symptoms: Blossom-end rot may occur in tomato
records.confirm: Review moisture consistency, salinity, roots and tissue analysis.

records.name: Magnesium deficiency
symptoms: Interveinal yellowing while veins stay greener
records.confirm: Use soil/tissue analysis and check potassium imbalance.
actions: Apply only a verified magnesium source

records.name: Sulfur deficiency
records.confirm: Compare leaf-age pattern with nitrogen deficiency and test.

records.name: Boron deficiency
records.confirm: Require soil/tissue analysis because the safe range is narrow.

records.name: Zinc deficiency
symptoms: Maize may show pale bands beside the midrib
records.confirm: Test soil/tissue zinc and review pH and phosphorus.
actions: Do not copy rates between products

records.name: Iron deficiency
symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis first on young leaves
Severe leaves may become nearly white
records.confirm: Check pH, waterlogging, root health and analysis.

records.name: Manganese deficiency
records.confirm: Use tissue analysis and review high pH or excessive liming.

records.name: Copper deficiency
symptoms: Twisted young leaves or shoot dieback
records.confirm: Confirm through analysis and review organic-matter conditions.
actions: Do not confuse with copper fungicide rates

records.name: Molybdenum deficiency
records.confirm: Check pH and tissue status.
actions: Correct acidic pH only from a lime requirement

records.name: Chloride deficiency / excess check
symptoms: Excess more often causes marginal scorch and salinity injury
records.confirm: Test soil and irrigation-water chloride.
actions: Treat drainage/salinity when excess is confirmed

records.name: Nickel deficiency
records.confirm: Require laboratory tissue analysis and specialist interpretation.
actions: Do not apply nickel from a photo

records.name: Salinity / sodium stress
records.confirm: Test EC, pH, exchangeable sodium and irrigation water.
actions: Do not apply gypsum without requirement

records.name: Water stress
records.confirm: Measure calibrated root-zone moisture and inspect roots/drainage.
actions: Calculate irrigation from area, root depth and deficit
